cohort: 177 primipara women who had delivered 2 years prior to the study in Sabzevar Hospitals, Iran
finding: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean) was not significantly associated with long-term female sexual function, urinary incontinence, or fecal incontinence.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in overall female sexual function scores (measured using the FSFI) between women who had a natural vaginal delivery and those who had a cesarean section (p=0.23).
